architecture: Simple NodeNext ESM TypeScript HTTP API using only node:http, node:crypto, and node:url. Files are disjoint: src/index.ts and src/support.ts for developer-a; src/store.ts for developer-b. createServer() creates a fresh in-memory TaskStore closure and returns an unstarted node:http Server. The HTTP handler implements POST /tasks, GET /tasks, GET /tasks/:id, and DELETE /tasks/:id; all other route or method combinations return 404 JSON. POST trims title, defaults completed to false, rejects malformed JSON, null/array bodies, non-object bodies, invalid title, and invalid completed with 400 JSON {error:string}; valid creation returns 201 JSON {id,title,completed}. Stored and returned titles are exactly the trimmed value. GET /tasks returns 200 insertion-order JSON array. GET /tasks/:id returns 200 task or 404 JSON error. DELETE /tasks/:id returns 204 empty body or 404 JSON error and removes the task. Error bodies are JSON objects with field error. IDs are nonempty unique randomUUID strings. Direct execution uses pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href and listens on PORT, default 3000 when PORT is undefined. T-001 and T-002 have no ticket dependencies and can start concurrently against the published interfaces.
interfaces: ESM NodeNext. Relative imports must use .js. src/index.ts exports: import type { Server } from 'node:http'; export function createServer(): Server. It must not call listen; each call has isolated storage. Direct-execution guard: if process.argv[1] and import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, then createServer().listen(process.env.PORT === undefined ? 3000 : Number(process.env.PORT)). src/index.ts consumes import { createTaskStore } from './store.js'; import { parseTaskInput, errorBody } from './support.js'. Published store interface in src/store.ts: export interface Task { id: string; title: string; completed: boolean } export interface TaskInput { title: string; completed: boolean } export interface TaskStore { create(input: TaskInput): Task; list(): Task[]; get(id: string): Task | undefined; delete(id: string): boolean } export function createTaskStore(): TaskStore. Store uses randomUUID from node:crypto; create stores {id,title:input.title,completed:input.completed}; list returns shallow copies in insertion order; get returns copy or undefined; delete removes and returns true iff present; instances isolated. Published reliability helper interface in src/support.ts: export interface NormalizedTaskInput { title: string; completed: boolean } export type ParseTaskInputResult = { ok: true; value: NormalizedTaskInput } | { ok: false; error: string }; export function parseTaskInput(value: unknown): ParseTaskInputResult; export function errorBody(message: string): { error: string }. parseTaskInput accepts only non-null non-array objects; title must be a string and trim to a nonempty string; returned value.title is the trimmed title; completed defaults false when absent; supplied completed must be boolean; extra fields ignored. NormalizedTaskInput is structurally compatible with TaskInput. HTTP observable behavior: POST /tasks malformed JSON or non-object/null/array body or parse failure -> 400 {error:string}; valid -> 201 {id,title,completed}. GET /tasks -> 200 JSON array insertion order. GET /tasks/:id -> 200 task or 404 {error:string}. DELETE /tasks/:id -> 204 empty body or 404 {error:string}. Unknown route or unsupported method on known path -> 404 {error:string}. JSON responses use application/json; charset=utf-8; no request Content-Type validation.

tickets.title: HTTP API server, routing, validation, and direct startup
tickets.description: Implement src/support.ts and src/index.ts. Build parseTaskInput and errorBody exactly as published, then create the HTTP server factory, routing, body parsing, normalization, status/error responses, and direct-execution listener. Use createTaskStore from ./store.js against the published interface; do not edit src/store.ts. Ensure title trimming and completed defaulting are enforced end to end for noncanonical valid inputs.

tickets.title: In-memory task store with unique IDs and insertion order
tickets.description: Implement src/store.ts with the published Task, TaskInput, TaskStore, and createTaskStore interface. Maintain a private array per store instance, generate randomUUID IDs, preserve insertion order, return shallow copies from list/get, and delete by ID. Do not edit src/index.ts or src/support.ts.
